subject: [hw] R1 finding F2 (V14, MEDIUM): MOV PC, Rm must be BXWritePC (interworking), not a plain branch
body:
File: gpu/hwcodec/emu/n2a32_t16.c:458-462 (t16_special, case 0x2).

ARM ARM MOV (register) T1 (encoding 0100 0110 DM Rm Rdn = 0x46xx): pseudocode is
  if d == 15 then BXWritePC(R[m]); else R[d] = R[m];
BXWritePC sets PSTATE.T from R[m]<0> and aligns the target. The code calls n2a32_branch(c, c->r[rs]) for Rdn==15, which keeps c->thumb unchanged. That is only correct while both sides are Thumb (LR odd). It is wrong for `mov pc, rN` where rN holds an ARM address (bit0=0): the interpreter stays in Thumb mode and executes ARM code as Thumb.

Repro (my spot test, review/r1/spot/spot.c):
  c.r[15]=0x1004; c.next_pc=0x1002; c.thumb=1; c.r[14]=0x100;
  n2a32_t16(&c, 0x46F7) /* mov pc, lr */
  current: rc=0 next_pc=0x100 thumb=1; expected per BXWritePC: thumb=0.
  (With LR=0x101 both implementations agree, which is why the tests pass.)

Fix: `if (rdn == 15u) n2a32_bx(c, c->r[rs]); else c->r[rdn] = c->r[rs];` and update the STATUS text that currently says ALU writes to PC use n2a32_branch. ADD PC, Rm is correctly n2a32_branch (ALUWritePC, no interworking) — keep that one.

Severity medium: vendor Thumb code compiled by clang returns with bx lr/pop {pc}, so this is not expected on the hot path, but it is an architectural deviation and a silent wrong-mode execution if hit. My spot run: 154/157 checks pass; the 3 failures are F1 (2) and this one.
